fragment_A.why: `within` requires only that SOME sample satisfies the predicate. Two earlier samples were null; that is eventual consistency, not a failure. An evaluator returning FAIL here has made `within` as strict as `hold`.

fragment_B.why: Polled to expiry, nothing matched, error is null. A probe that ran and returned nothing is a product signal: FAIL, not INFRA.

harness_findings.detail: The poll stopped 26000ms short of expiry. The FAIL stands, but it is not evidence that the predicate was false for the declared budget.

fragment_C.why: Verdicts may be weakened, never strengthened. A truncated poll can only manufacture a false red, so FAIL survives — but the truncation must be reported, or the suite silently redefines its own budgets.

conformance_note: An evaluator that returns the same verdict for fragment A as case 002 fragment A has collapsed `within` into `hold`. An evaluator that returns INDETERMINATE for fragment C has treated missing evidence for a red as an unknown; it is not — see method/02-verdicts.md.
